pullRequest.bodyHTML:
Closes #161.

The queue ran its front sync to the end, so the open Repository's timed refresh waited behind a first sync of CPython, and a new PR took 12 minutes to show. Now each queued sync takes one step at a time. The open Repository gets every other step, and the others take theirs in the order you asked for them. A step that saves sends changed at once, so the Workbench shows a refresh's first batch while CPython still syncs.

A failure that speaks for all of GitHub (Offline, a rate limit, certificate dates, Unauthorized) still holds back every step. Any other failure holds back only its own Repository until the next status refresh, and counts toward that sync's 10 tries. If that Repository isn't the open one, the status bar message starts with its name. An Issue fetch that fails holds back no sync, unless all of GitHub is out.

SyncActivity now carries the open Repository's progress under open, and lists the other Repositories syncing in elsewhere, sorted by name so the turns don't reorder it. The status bar shows them beside the sync time: Synced 3 min ago · python/peps syncing, or python/peps and 2 more syncing.

ADR 0015 gains a paragraph on the turns and a considered option: the open Repository's sync first, to its end. The CHANGELOG's WIP section gets a Fixed entry.

Tests: the Syncs methods against the Harness with recorded replies, for the order of turns, a refresh beside another sync, the two kinds of hold, the activity and a named failure. StatusBar and synced.ts tests cover the words. just check passes on Windows.
